title: Post-incident stabilization plan for failed traffic-split experiment and automated rollback gaps
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: A staged A/B traffic-split test that promoted a quantized model variant to 10% traffic caused a visible latency and error spike for a subset of customers. Automatic rollback did not trigger as expected because critical telemetry tags were not propagated from the routing layer to the telemetry pipeline, and the rollback heuristics were evaluating a filtered metric set. This ticket captures the incident follow-ups: immediate stabilizing actions taken, root cause analysis, and the set of runbook+automation changes to prevent recurrence.
impact_summary: ~8% of production requests experienced 2x increased p95 latency and a 0.7% rise in user-facing 5xx errors during the 26-minute window. Several internal dashboards alerted but the automation that should have initiated rollback remained idle due to metric dropouts for the canary traffic namespace.
investigation_summary: Key findings: (1) The traffic-split introduced model_variant=quant-8 tag at the router level but an intermediary proxy stripped the tag before metrics ingestion. (2) The auto-rollback circuit evaluates 'service.errors.v1' filtered by tag 'deployment.zone' and 'route', so the canary-specific error signals were missing. (3) The hysteresis window for rollback required a sustained signal across two minutes; short spikes were therefore ignored. (4) KV-cache collisions between old and quantized model variants exacerbated latency for warm-start requests on P100 nodes.
timeline: 2026-03-09T15:02Z: Canary rollout started (10% traffic to quant-8 variant)
2026-03-09T15:08Z: First internal latency alert on per-route dashboard (p95 increase)
2026-03-09T15:12Z: Error rate spikes observed by SRE but not tagged to canary namespace; alert routed to oncall
2026-03-09T15:18Z: Oncall opened incident; attempted manual rollback but runbook showed rollback automation inactive for this metric scope
2026-03-09T15:28Z: Manual traffic split returned to 0% for quant-8; metrics returned to baseline by 15:34Z
2026-03-09T16:00Z: Post-incident conference call convened with runtime, routing, telemetry, and SRE owners
root_cause: Telemetry-tag mismatch and circuit-breaker semantics. An intermediary egress proxy (edge-proxy-2) removed model_variant tags added by the router. The rollback automation filters excluded the traffic-split namespace, so the error/latency signals from the canary were invisible to the automation. Secondary contributing cause: KV-cache keyspace overlap worsened tail latency for quantized variant on certain serving nodes.
immediate_actions_taken: Manually reverted traffic split for quant-8 to 0% at 2026-03-09T15:28Z
Restarted affected serving pods to flush KV cache and clear keyspace collisions
Added temporary dashboard highlighting untagged error counts across all routes for investigation
Applied emergency rule to route-by-header until proxy preserves telemetry tags
followup_work: Ensure router -> edge proxy -> telemetry pipeline preserves model_variant and traffic-split tags end-to-end
Revise auto-rollback filters to include fallback detection (unattributed error spikes on relevant routes)
Isolate KV cache namespaces per model variant in runtime to prevent collisions during staged rollouts
Introduce a preflight synthetic canary that validates telemetry propagation before any production traffic split
Create e2e test to validate rollback automation activation against synthetic signals
runbook_changes: Add step: preflight telemetry smoke check (validate model_variant tags flow through metrics/trace/log pipelines).
Add step: if telemetry-tag validation fails, abort rollout automatically and notify deployment channel
Clarify manual rollback path when automation does not fire (exact api calls and IAM role required),
Document KV-cache isolation procedure and cron to verify per-variant hit rates
Add RACI table for routing/proxy/telemetry owners in rollout runbook
telemetry_and_alerting_changes: Create a new metric 'rollout.unattributed_errors' computed as delta between route-level errors and tag-filtered errors
Create alert: rollout.unattributed_errors > 0.5% for 2m => P0 oncall
Instrument router to emit a telemetry heartbeat with route+variant tags every 30s
Add a canary-specific dashboard with both raw and tag-filtered metrics and p95/p99 latency views
automation_and_policy_proposals: Rollback logic: prefer p95 latency + user-facing error rate; evaluate both global and tag-filtered metrics and fall back to unattributed detection
Shorten hysteresis window for rollback to 60s for early-stage canaries and increase to 3m for >20% traffic
Add automatic KV-cache isolation toggle in runtime during traffic-split experiments
Require telemetry propagation check as a gating policy in the rollout orchestration system
test_plan: Unit tests for tag propagation through edge-proxy-2 (PR ready: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1421)
Integration: deploy canary to staging with observability pipeline mirroring production and validate detection and rollback within 90s
Chaos test: synthetic KV-cache collision injected into staging canary to assert circuit-breaker behavior
Runbook drill: simulate automation failure and measure manual rollback time; target <5 minutes
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry tags preserved end-to-end and verified by synthetic preflight
Rollback automation triggers for synthetic canary failure in staging within 90s
KV-cache isolation per variant implemented and validated on staging
Runbook updated and oncall trained (drill completed)

notes: This incident highlights a class of failures where telemetry contract mismatches mask automation signals. Prevention requires both tech fixes and operational changes (preflight, runbook clarity, and drills). Treat telemetry propagation as a first-class rollout dependency going forward.
